question: The process in which an oil pump housing is first filled with oil, especially for oil pumps that are driven by the crankshaft, is known as:

options.text: priming of a new oil pump

solution:
The correct answer is __Priming of a new oil pump__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Priming__ is the process of filling the oil pump housing with oil before use.
 
• It is particularly important for oil pumps driven by the crankshaft to ensure proper lubrication.
 
• Priming helps avoid dry running and ensures the pump operates efficiently.
 
• This process is crucial to prevent cavitation or damage to the pump.
 
• The oil pump must be primed correctly during installation or replacement to ensure smooth operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Cavitation:**

 
 
• It refers to the formation of air bubbles within the pump, which can cause damage.
 
• Occurs due to insufficient lubrication or improper priming.
 
 
 
• **Ferrography:**
 
 
• Ferrography is a diagnostic technique used to analyze wear particles in lubricants.
 
• It helps identify the condition of mechanical systems and detect potential failures.
 
 
 
• **Alignment:**
 
 
• Proper alignment of a pump ensures that it operates without undue strain or wear.
 
• Misalignment can cause inefficiency and mechanical damage.
